DESCRIPTION: Patient is concerned about insurance coverage or out-of-pocket costs for durable medical equipment.
ROUTING_NOTE: If equipment is not delivered or not set up, code under Care Coordination And Follow Up.

DESCRIPTION: Patient cannot afford copays for physical therapy, cardiac rehabilitation, or outpatient therapy services.
Patient cannot afford copays for clinic visits or follow-up appointments, leading to delayed evaluation.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the cost barrier is for medications, use Medication Cost Barrier.

DESCRIPTION: Housing is unstable, unsafe, or unsuitable for recovery (crowding, stairs, lack of bed, unsafe layout).
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is specifically environmental hazards like mold or lack of heat, use Unsafe Home Environment Conditions.

DESCRIPTION: Patient cannot reliably obtain foods compatible with prescribed diet due to cost, transportation, or availability.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is confusion about diet rules rather than access, use Diet Restrictions Clarification Needed.

DESCRIPTION: Patient lacks help at home for self-care tasks, equipment setup, or safe mobility during recovery.
ROUTING_NOTE: If home health services were ordered but not started, use Home Health Services Not Started.

DESCRIPTION: Home environment problems such as mold, water damage, extreme temperatures, or utility failures affecting health and recovery.
Call content is primarily administrative, such as paperwork, contact details or program questions, with no clinical, medication or care coordination issue raised.
Patient or caregiver requested a callback at a different time and assessment was deferred.
Patient could not be reached or did not meaningfully engage in assessment.
Patient reports no concerns and the call documents a stable status check only.
Patient explicitly declined follow-up participation or requested removal from the program.
Call reached someone but patient was not available and assessment could not be performed.
Phone number was wrong, disconnected, or otherwise prevented reaching the patient.
Insurance explanation of benefits, billing questions, or suspected billing errors unrelated to medication access.
ROUTING_NOTE: Use Medication Coverage Or Prior Authorization Delay when the issue prevents obtaining a medication; use this subtheme when the issue is billing paperwork or charges.

DESCRIPTION: Notes primarily about updating demographics or contact information (phone, address) rather than clinical follow-up.
Duplicate charts, duplicate discharge paperwork, or incorrect encounter records requiring reconciliation.
Conflicting or unclear post-discharge instructions require clarification from the surgical or medical team.
ROUTING_NOTE: When the confusion is specifically about diet, route to Diet And Nutrition Guidance; when specifically about wound care steps, route to Wound Care Instructions.

DESCRIPTION: Patient has not received a follow-up appointment or does not know how to schedule it.
A referral was given but the specialty appointment or referral processing is incomplete or missing.
Patient is unable to reach the surgeon, primary care, or specialist office despite attempts.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the access problem is specifically about insurance network or copay barriers, use Financial And Insurance Barriers instead.

DESCRIPTION: Home health or visiting nurse services were ordered but have not started as expected.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the primary issue is missing wound supplies rather than missing visits, use Wound Care Supplies Not Delivered.

DESCRIPTION: Patient needs post-discharge durable medical equipment support from the supplier or clinician.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is inability to pay for equipment, use Medical Equipment Cost Concern.

DESCRIPTION: Physical therapy, occupational therapy, or rehabilitation needs are not arranged or require re-evaluation.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the barrier is inability to afford therapy copays, use Therapy Copay Barrier.

DESCRIPTION: Patient received confusing, duplicate, or inconsistent discharge documents and needs help reconciling them.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the note focuses on duplicate medical record numbers or duplicate charts, use Duplicate Record Identified.

DESCRIPTION: Patient is waiting on results of inpatient tests or labs and needs status or explanation.
Bleeding concern in the setting of anticoagulant use or INR monitoring questions.
ROUTING_NOTE: Use Postoperative Site Bleeding Or Bruising if the issue is localized to incision bruising/oozing rather than anticoagulation management.

DESCRIPTION: Black stools, dark tarry stools, or melena symptoms suggesting gastrointestinal bleeding.
ROUTING_NOTE: If bleeding is described at the surgical site, use Postoperative Site Bleeding Or Bruising.

DESCRIPTION: Vomiting described as coffee grounds or containing blood, suggesting upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Chest pain, pressure, tightness, or discomfort with or without exertion.
ROUTING_NOTE: If clearly described as incisional pain at sternotomy or chest incision, use Postoperative Incision Pain under Postoperative Pain; otherwise treat as cardiopulmonary symptom.

DESCRIPTION: Leg or ankle swelling, rapid weight gain, or fluid retention symptoms not limited to the surgical site.
ROUTING_NOTE: If swelling is described only as expected localized post-op swelling at a knee incision, code under Postoperative Orthopedic Recovery Concerns when appropriate; otherwise use this subtheme.

DESCRIPTION: Palpitations, heart racing, skipped beats, or irregular heartbeat sensations.
Shortness of breath at rest or with exertion, new or worsening compared with baseline after discharge.
Loose stools, diarrhea, frequent bowel movements, or suspected antibiotic-associated diarrhea.
ROUTING_NOTE: If stool is dark tarry or black, use Black Tarry Stool Melena.

DESCRIPTION: Nausea, queasiness, or upset stomach with or without reduced intake when vomiting is not the main feature.
ROUTING_NOTE: If vomiting is frequent or primary, use Vomiting Episodes; if linked to diet advancement after GI surgery, use Diet Advancement Intolerance under Patient Education.

DESCRIPTION: New abdominal pain not primarily at the incision site, including cramping or post-prandial abdominal pain.
ROUTING_NOTE: If pain is clearly at the incision and post-op, use Postoperative Incision Pain or Generalized Postoperative Pain.

DESCRIPTION: Any vomiting episodes post-discharge, including intermittent or frequent emesis.
ROUTING_NOTE: If emesis is described as coffee ground, use Coffee Ground Or Bloody Vomit.

DESCRIPTION: Fever, chills, sweats, or elevated temperature reported without a primary wound complaint.
ROUTING_NOTE: If fever is tied to an incision concern, use Systemic Infection Concern Postoperative.

DESCRIPTION: Generalized fatigue, weakness, or low energy affecting daily function, not primarily pain-related.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the weakness is primarily balance or near-fall complaints, use Dizziness Or Near Syncope.

DESCRIPTION: New confusion, disorientation, getting lost, or acute mental status change compared with baseline.
Dizziness, lightheadedness, near-syncope, or balance instability with near falls.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the main issue is equipment setup or mobility training rather than symptoms, use Mobility Equipment Use Difficulty.

DESCRIPTION: Tingling, numbness, or paresthesia symptoms not described as expected post-op localized nerve symptoms.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the note explicitly links onset to a new medication and frames as side effect, use Possible Medication Side Effect.

DESCRIPTION: Tremor, shaking, or involuntary movements not present prior to discharge.
ROUTING_NOTE: If clearly linked to a new medication, use Possible Medication Side Effect.

DESCRIPTION: Patient is taking less than prescribed (skipping, every other day) specifically to make medication last due to cost.
Patient reports the medication cost or copay is unaffordable, leading to nonfill or delayed start.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the patient is already stretching doses or skipping doses because of cost, use Cost Related Dose Rationing.

SUBTHEME: Medication Coverage Or Prior Authorization Delay
DESCRIPTION: Medication cannot be filled due to prior authorization, coverage adjudication, or insurer approval delay.
Patient requests a refill, replacement, or extension of medication supply unrelated to insurance denial.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is that the medication was never received by the pharmacy, use Prescription Not At Pharmacy.

DESCRIPTION: Pharmacy reports the prescription was not received, missing, or not on file.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the prescription exists but insurance is blocking coverage, use Medication Coverage Or Prior Authorization Delay.

DESCRIPTION: Patient is unsure how to take the medication (dose, timing, with food) or reports missing instructions.
Patient has the medication but has not started it due to hesitation, preference, or waiting to feel better.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the reason is confusion about directions rather than reluctance, use Medication Directions Unclear.

DESCRIPTION: Discharge medication list conflicts with the patient’s home regimen and requires reconciliation.
Patient reports suspected side effects from a medication (new symptom temporally linked to a medication).
ROUTING_NOTE: If the symptom is potentially emergent (e.g., chest pain, severe dyspnea), code the symptom under Clinical Symptoms and add secondary medication review outside taxonomy if needed.

DESCRIPTION: Patient needs guidance on activity restrictions such as lifting, driving, return to work, or resuming normal activities.
Patient is not performing instructed monitoring such as daily weights, blood pressure checks, or similar tracking.
Patient or caregiver requests guidance on when to call the surgeon, primary care, or emergency services for red flags.
Patient cannot tolerate prescribed diet advancement after surgery (clear to full to soft) due to nausea or discomfort.
ROUTING_NOTE: If nausea is present without explicit diet advancement issue, use Nausea Without Vomiting under Clinical Symptoms.

DESCRIPTION: Patient is confused about diet restrictions, allowable foods, or conflicting dietary guidance post-discharge.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the primary barrier is inability to afford or obtain appropriate foods, use Limited Access To Appropriate Foods.

DESCRIPTION: Patient needs assistance with home glucose meter use or inability to obtain consistent readings.
ROUTING_NOTE: If this is about obtaining supplies due to cost or coverage, code under Financial And Insurance Barriers instead.

DESCRIPTION: Patient needs help using mobility aids such as walker, crutches, or adjusting equipment for safety.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the primary complaint is dizziness or near-syncope rather than equipment mechanics, use Dizziness Or Near Syncope.

DESCRIPTION: Patient needs help using home medical devices such as CPAP, nebulizer, or related respiratory equipment.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is obtaining equipment or coverage rather than use, code under Medical Equipment Cost Concern or Care Coordination themes.

DESCRIPTION: Difficulty transferring, walking, climbing stairs, or weakness limiting mobility after surgery.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the problem is mainly unsteady feeling with dizziness/near falls, use Dizziness Or Near Syncope.

DESCRIPTION: Patient reports musculoskeletal cramps or myalgias after discharge, often suspected medication-related.
ROUTING_NOTE: If explicitly framed as a medication side effect request (e.g., statin cramps), use Possible Medication Side Effect.

DESCRIPTION: Concerns specific to orthopedic recovery (knee arthroplasty) such as weight-bearing pain or range-of-motion limitation without infection signs.
ROUTING_NOTE: If incision shows redness/warmth/drainage or opening, code wound concerns under Postoperative Wound And Device Concerns.

DESCRIPTION: Pain described as diffuse, generalized, or not localized to the incision or operative site after surgery.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the pain is new abdominal pain unrelated to surgery, use Non Incisional Abdominal Pain under Clinical Symptoms.

DESCRIPTION: Patient reports prescribed pain regimen is not controlling pain or needs adjustment/reevaluation.
ROUTING_NOTE: Use this when the primary issue is inadequate analgesia; use Postoperative Incision Pain or Generalized Postoperative Pain as primary when location/type is the key point and analgesia adequacy is not the focus.

DESCRIPTION: Need for clarification on whether to take medications for pain or how to use them safely as prescribed.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is access to pain medication due to missing prescription or cost, use Medication Access And Coverage subthemes.

DESCRIPTION: Pain localized to an incision or operative site where infection signs are denied or not the focus.
ROUTING_NOTE: If redness/warmth/drainage is present, code wound concerns under Postoperative Wound And Device Concerns rather than pain.

DESCRIPTION: Concerns about chest tube sites after cardiothoracic surgery, including weeping or drainage at the tube site.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the site is described as purulent or clearly infected, use Purulent Wound Drainage Suspected Infection.

DESCRIPTION: Questions about compression stockings, compression garments, or related post-op compression equipment.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is swelling without equipment questions, use Leg Or Ankle Swelling under Clinical Symptoms.

DESCRIPTION: Questions about care, output, color change, or removal timing for a surgical drain.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the concern is explicitly about infection at drain site with purulence, use Purulent Wound Drainage Suspected Infection.

DESCRIPTION: Questions about wound vacuum therapy use, troubleshooting, or coverage planning for wound vacuum supplies.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the issue is only about insurance coverage cost, use Medical Equipment Cost Concern.

DESCRIPTION: Patient is unsure how to change dressings, clean incision, or perform routine wound care steps.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the main issue is not receiving supplies or visits, use Wound Care Supplies Not Delivered or Home Health Services Not Started.

DESCRIPTION: Patient reports ordered wound supplies (gauze, saline, dressing kits) were not delivered or ran out without replacement plan.
Redness, warmth, swelling, or tenderness at an incision without explicit drainage described.
ROUTING_NOTE: If purulent, yellow, green, or foul drainage is described, use Purulent Wound Drainage Suspected Infection.

DESCRIPTION: Drainage described as pus, yellow or green fluid, foul drainage, or weeping concerning for infection.
Fever or chills reported in the context of a post-operative wound concern (even if incision looks normal).
ROUTING_NOTE: If fever is reported without any wound discussion, use Fever Or Chills Under Clinical Symptoms.

DESCRIPTION: Bleeding, persistent bruising, or oozing at or near the surgical site raising concern for hemorrhage.
ROUTING_NOTE: If the bleeding is described as dark stools or coffee ground emesis, use Gastrointestinal Bleeding Signs under Clinical Symptoms.

DESCRIPTION: Incision edges separating, wound opening, staples or sutures pulling apart, or dehiscence concern.
